title: Note On/Off per electrode
statement: Each of the 12 electrode inputs E0–E11 (MPR121 ELE0–ELE11) shall send one MIDI Note On, on the configured channel (default 1) with the configured fixed velocity (default 100, range 1–127), when a touch is detected. It shall send a Note Off for the same note when the touch is released.
evidence: I: PASS. The chain terminal → series resistor → module electrode is 1:1 (interface_check `pcb.A2.pin2..13`, `pcb.J2.*`). T: NOT RUN.

title: Note Off integrity
statement: The Note Off for a pad shall carry the note number sent in its Note On, even if the scale or octave changed in between. All sounding notes shall be released before a recalibration.
evidence: Host tests PASS (T-044 handoff, 295 host tests passed). Hardware test NOT RUN.

title: Second sensor (24 pads)
statement: The firmware shall support a second MPR121 at I2C address 0x5B (`NUM_SENSORS = 2`), mapping its electrodes to pads 12–23. This is a breadboard-only option; the PCB carries one module (ADR-007 D-3).
evidence: A: latency PASS at 400 kHz (12.35 ms ≤ 15 ms, jitter 8.35 ms), using the worst-case run-based burst plan (budgets.out §b). T: NOT RUN.

title: Polyphonic aftertouch
statement: While a pad is touched, the device shall send Polyphonic Key Pressure (0xAn) with a value 0–127. The value shall map linearly from delta = baseline − filtered, clamped to [12, 120]. It shall be evaluated every 15 ms and sent only when it changes by at least 2.
evidence: Host tests PASS (T-044 handoff, 295 host tests passed). Aftertouch messages are sent after all Note On/Off of the same loop (ADR-010). Hardware NOT RUN.

title: Six scales
statement: The device shall provide 6 scales, selected cyclically: Drum Rack (36–47, octave ignored, the power-on default), major pentatonic, minor pentatonic, major, natural minor and chromatic (root 48). Notes shall be clamped to 0–127.
evidence: A: notes 24–99 with 12 pads and 24–127 with 24 pads, never clamped (T-009 budgets §d). Host tests PASS (T-040 `test_scales.py`).

title: Octave potentiometer
statement: The octave potentiometer (off-board on 3 wires, ADR-023 D-2) shall shift melodic scales by −2..+2 octaves using 5 ADC zones, each V33/5 = 0.660 V wide. The octave shall change only when the reading is more than 0.7 zone from the current zone centre, i.e. 0.2 zone (0.132 V) beyond the border, which is the dead band. The combined ADC noise, DNL, quantisation and supply ripple shall stay below the dead band. A static ADC offset shifts every threshold together and does not consume the dead band. The pot shall have no effect on Drum Rack and shall be enabled by default on the PCB build.
evidence: A: PASS. Error budget 0.0364 V < dead band 0.132 V, margin 0.096 V (budgets A5). Inputs: noise from ENOB 8.7 (SOURCE S-17 Table 627); DNL peak 10 LSB12 (ASSUMPTION; S-17 §4.9.4 and erratum RP2040-E11 give peaks at codes 512/1536/2560/3584, height only in a figure); 10-bit step; ripple 10 mV (ASSUMPTION). The nearest DNL-peak code is 0.049 V from a switch point. The static offset of about 30 mV (S-01 §4.3) is reported, not budgeted (review F-003). Host tests PASS (T-043). RV1 is the Bourns PTV09A-4015F-B103, 10 kΩ ±20 % linear, insulated flatted shaft (SOURCE T96-S2/T96-S3, ADR-024/T-096), with knob SPK-016A (bore fit NOT CONFIRMED). The EE check calc_pot_rc gives ADC loading ≤ 14.9 counts PASS, residual resistance 6.25 % PASS and settling 2.89 ms (CALCULATION, T-096). C1 wiper filter (ADR-021, ADR-023): 100 nF X7R 1206, Samsung CL31B104KBCNNNC (187-CL31B104KBCNNNC) from POT to AGND; worst Thevenin source 3.0 kOhm (10 kOhm +20 %, SOURCE T96-S3, mid travel) and worst C 126.5 nF (+10 % tolerance, +15 % X7R temperature; ASSUMPTION, the Samsung datasheet was not opened) give tau 0.380 ms and settling to 1/2 LSB at 10 bits in 2.89 ms against the 30 ms read period (SOURCE fm_pot.h POT_READ_MS), margin 10.4x (CALCULATION, budgets A7 PASS, criterion 5x ASSUMPTION). Off-board wiring (ADR-023 D-2), budgets A8 PASS: 0.50 m at 50 pF/m adds 25 pF to C1 (0.028 % of 90 nF), and the IR drop is 26.8 uV per wire at 0.41 mA and 0.13 Ohm/m against the 0.132 V dead band (CALCULATION; length, capacitance and resistance per metre are ASSUMPTIONS). Hum and interference pickup on the wires is NOT RUN (not analysed); risk R-011 covers ESD on the wires. C1 does not enter the error budget, which keeps the 10 mV ripple ASSUMPTION. Hardware NOT RUN.

title: Button short press
statement: A short press of the button (released within 800 ms, sampled every 10 ms) shall select the next scale, and the LED shall blink N times for scale N.
evidence: Host tests PASS (T-044 handoff, 295 host tests passed). Hardware NOT RUN.

title: Button long press recalibration
statement: A press of more than 800 ms shall release all notes and recalibrate all sensors; the LED then blinks 3 times.
evidence: Host tests PASS (T-044 handoff, 295 host tests passed). Recalibration blocks for 16.8–22.1 ms per sensor at 400 kHz (CALCULATION); this is user-requested and allowed by REQ-016. Hardware NOT RUN.

title: Sensor absent or lost
statement: If no MPR121 answers at start, the device shall send no MIDI from it and retry. During play, a sensor shall be marked lost after 3 consecutive failed I2C transactions, or at once when its ECR read-back (every 250 ms) differs from the value read after start-up (a chip that reset itself). On loss the firmware shall release that sensor's notes, show the fast error blink and stop reading it. It shall retry start-up when more than 2 s have passed since the last start attempt (this also covers a second sensor missing at boot). The other sensor shall keep playing.
evidence: Host tests PASS: `tests/firmware/logic/test_notes_health.py` (15 tests), within `295 passed` (T-044 handoff). Implementation: `fm_notes.h`/health logic, `startSensor()` = begin → setClock(400000) → configure → ECR read. A self-reset chip releases its notes through the normal touch path before the ECR check, so only one Note Off is sent. Physical NOT RUN (it needs the sensor unplugged or reset during play).

title: Status LED
statement: The LED shall give 2 slow blinks at start when a sensor is found, and shall be lit while any pad is touched. On Pico W and Pico 2 W the LED is driven through the CYW43 (WL_GPIO0).

title: USB MIDI class compliance
statement: The device shall enumerate as a USB MIDI 1.0 class device (MIDIStreaming, bulk endpoints). It shall work without vendor drivers on Windows 10, Windows 11 and macOS 12 or later.

title: Device name
statement: The USB product string and the MIDI port name shall be "FrutaMIDI".
evidence: I: `DEVICE_NAME = "FrutaMIDI"` is passed to `setProductDescriptor` and `setStringDescriptor`. T: NOT RUN.

title: MIDI message set
statement: The device shall send only Note On (0x9n, CIN 0x9), Note Off (0x8n, velocity 0, CIN 0x8) and Polyphonic Key Pressure (0xAn, CIN 0xA), on one channel n = MIDI_CHANNEL − 1. Incoming MIDI shall be read and discarded.
evidence: `fm_midi.h` constants match S-14 Table 4-1.

title: Touch-to-MIDI latency
statement: Device latency from the first touch after a pad has been idle for at least 15 ms (DEBOUNCE_MS) to the USB-MIDI packet being available to the host shall be ≤ 15 ms worst case, for electrode capacitance ≤ 100 pF, with mitigation M1 (one burst read per sensor per aftertouch pass). A re-touch of the same pad within the 15 ms lockout is outside this requirement and is reported separately.
evidence: A: PASS. 1 sensor 10.72 ms, 2 sensors 12.35 ms at 400 kHz, including the T-044 ECR poll (≈ 0.14 ms per sensor) (CALCULATION, budgets.out §b). Separate term: a re-touch inside the lockout adds up to 15 ms, giving 25.72 ms worst case (review F-011). Design limit C ≤ 210 pF. T: NOT RUN (plan item P-2). Flagged for user review (ADR-007).

title: Latency jitter
statement: Latency jitter (worst minus best) shall be ≤ 10 ms for electrode capacitance ≤ 100 pF.
evidence: A: PASS. 6.72 ms (1 sensor) and 8.35 ms (2 sensors) at 400 kHz, including the ECR poll (CALCULATION). T: NOT RUN.

title: No blocking during play
statement: During play, no firmware action other than a user-requested recalibration or the automatic restart of a lost sensor shall block touch processing for more than 10 ms.
evidence: I: only delay(10) in midiBegin() (setup); non-blocking LED (fm_blink.h). A: worst loop ~1.72 ms, 1 sensor, 400 kHz (sim/systems/budgets.out, CALCULATION). Exception: lost-sensor restart 16.8-22.1 ms per retry, >=2 s apart (review N-001, ADR-018).

title: USB bus power only
statement: The device shall be powered only from USB VBUS through the Pico's micro-USB connector. No other power input shall exist.
evidence: Pico pins 39 and 40 are unconnected (`pcb.A1.no_other_nets`).

title: VBUS range
statement: The device shall operate with VBUS from 4.40 V to 5.50 V at its connector.
evidence: A: VSYS 3.95–5.25 V, inside the 1.8–5.5 V range (S-01 §2.1): PASS. However, the 4.40 V low-power-port minimum (S-10) is below the Pico's recommended VBUS of 5 V ± 10 % = 4.50 V (S-01 §2.3): budgets check A3b FAIL, so the requirement as stated FAILs (review F-010). Electrically the Pico still runs (VSYS margin 2.15 V). Options: restrict the statement to 4.50–5.50 V, or accept as a documented deviation. T: NOT RUN.

title: VBUS current
statement: VBUS current shall be ≤ 100 mA (the declared bMaxPower, S-11) for every supported Pico board.
evidence: A: worst case 55.6 / 70.6 / 60.6 / 75.6 mA for Pico / Pico W / Pico 2 / Pico 2 W. Lower bounds are SOURCE (S-01 Table 3, S-16 Table 2); RP2040 pull-ups 50–80 kΩ are SOURCE S-17. The upper bounds are ASSUMPTIONs. T: NOT RUN (plan item P-3).

title: 3V3 rail load
statement: The external load on the Pico 3V3(OUT) shall be ≤ 300 mA with at least 50 % margin.
evidence: 10.15 mA worst case with 2 sensors and PCB pull-ups: 96.6 % margin.

title: MPR121 supply voltage
statement: The MPR121 VDD, fed from the Pico 3V3 through the module LDO, shall be within 2.0–3.6 V.
evidence: 3.10–3.40 V (CALCULATION; dropout and rail tolerance are ASSUMPTIONs).

title: Touchable voltage (SELV)
statement: Every user-touchable conductor shall be at ≤ 3.6 V relative to GND and shall be supplied only from the USB SELV source.
evidence: Electrodes are charged from MPR121 VDD ≤ 3.6 V (S-04), and REQ-017 holds.

title: Electrode ESD robustness
statement: Each user-touched electrode terminal shall survive ±4 kV contact discharge without permanent damage. The ±4 kV target is an ASSUMPTION, following IEC 61000-4-2 level 2 (the standard was not read).
evidence: Estimate on ASSUMPTIONs, not a PASS (review F-002). Pulse capability of the fitted part is NOT PROVEN and the user accepted that (ADR-026), so this requirement stays PARTIAL at best until the test. v1.3 design (ADR-023 D-1, ADR-026; sim/electronics/calc/check_gap.out, calc_pulse_rated.out, calc_gnd_bounce.out, sim_electrode.out). Part: R1–R12 are YAGEO RC2512FK-073K3L (3k3 ±1 %, 1 W, 2512; Mouser 603-RC2512FK-073K3L, SOURCE T96-S0b) on footprint FrutaMIDI:R_2512_HomeEtch_G5.0mm (T-098 rename, land unchanged; interface_check `pcb.R1_R12_*` and pcb_rules_check `ADR-026 R1-R12 on footprint` PASS, mutation-tested T-099). Current: 4 kV / (3.3 kΩ + 330 Ω IEC source) = 1.10 A, 1.11 A at −1 % (3267 Ω), against the 1.33 A pin limit inferred from the HBM ±2 kV rating (the limit is itself an ASSUMPTION), margin 1.20–1.22 (CALCULATION); 2.20 A at 8 kV (FAIL). The margin compares peak current only: the 4 kV strike carries 600 nC against 200 nC for HBM 2 kV (3.0×) and decays with τ 0.54 µs against 0.15 µs (3.6×) (CALCULATION, review F3-005; stated beside the margin in hardware/README.md and reports/electronics/analysis.md section 8.3), so the peak-current margin understates the stress and is not a proof. Sensitivity with 3k3 ±1 %: worst ratio 0.904 at 3267/3300/3333 Ω against the 0.90 limit (SIMULATION, sim_electrode, PASS). Voltage across R: 3636 V at 4 kV, 7273 V at 8 kV; energy 1.09 / 4.36 mJ, τ 0.54 µs (CALCULATION). The YAGEO data give no pulse rating: 3.6 kV is 7.3× the 500 V overload voltage and 18× the 200 V working voltage (SOURCE YAGEO RC_L V.11, T96-S0); the old 182 mJ energy criterion is 167× one strike but is not a proof (calc_pulse_rated: `RC2512FK-073K3L pulse capability at IEC 4 kV: NOT PROVEN`). Flashover around R (gap rule ≥ 3.5 mm at 4 kV, ≥ 7.5 mm at 8 kV; CALCULATION on ASSUMPTION models; IEC 60664-1 F.2 recalled, not opened): (a) copper ELEx–Ex 5.00 mm and (b) Ex to other MPR121/Pico nets 5.29 mm (MEASUREMENT on the design file; land gap also pcb_rules_check `REQ-023 R1-R12 land gap` PASS 5.0 mm, 12 parts); (d) chip terminations (L 6.35 ±0.10, I1 0.60 ±0.20 mm SOURCE YAGEO RC_L V.11; placement error ASSUMPTION): worst 4.65 / 4.54 / 4.08 mm at 0 / ±0.25 / ±0.5 mm (CALCULATION); (e) mounting-metal bypass 8.40 mm (CALCULATION, T-092 holes). All PASS at 4 kV; (a), (b) and (d) FAIL at 8 kV. Ex to GND edge track 1.40 mm at every J2 pad (MEASUREMENT, pcb_rules_check `ADR-020` PASS, mutation-tested): the intentional spark gap (ADR-020), which arcs before the 5 mm gap around R. Module GND to Pico GND bounce up to 330 V for about 1 ns, ≤ 1.49 A and ≤ 0.90 nC per I²C line through R15/R16 (CALCULATION on ASSUMED inductances, T-103: taller module pin path 5.0–8.5 nH; was 236 V); 0.56× the peak and 0.2 % of the charge of the RP2040 HBM 4 kV FT-pin equivalent (budgets D1 PASS on that criterion). RP2040 HBM 4 kV rating stated for digital FT pins only; no rating found for GP26/GP27 (NOT CONFIRMED, EE-S28): risk R-010. 8 kV: risk R-006, scope stays ±4 kV. Plan B (T-097, not adopted): 12 × Bourns CDSOD323-T05LC (652-CDSOD323-T05LC, 1.0 pF typ, 5 µA) to GND with R1–R12 at 1 kΩ; sensitivity 0.938 PASS at 1 kΩ, 0.897 FAIL at 3k3 (SIMULATION); +6.18 EUR; before adoption confirm the maximum C_d and the leakage at 3.3 V. Trigger: risk R-018, accepted by the manager (ADR-027 D-2). RV1 Bourns PTV09A-4015F-B103 (off-board, insulated flatted shaft, SOURCE T96-S2/T96-S3) with knob SPK-016A (bore fit NOT CONFIRMED): the V1.2 hard copper link from the frame to AGND is gone; a metal shaft would not be protected (internal gap 0.5–2 mm ASSUMPTION, below the 3.5 mm rule; no series R on the three wires; C1 holds a wiper strike to about 6 V at 4 kV, CALCULATION, order of magnitude, calc_r011_offboard_pot.out, does not prove the ADC pad survives): controlled by the insulated shaft and insulating knob (hardware/README.md) and risk R-011. T: NOT RUN [PHYSICAL]. Plan: (1) before the test, measure the resistance of every R1–R12 (expected 3267–3333 Ω) and the body length L and termination length I1 of one part with a caliper; inside the analysed range if 6.25 ≤ L ≤ 6.45 mm and 0.40 ≤ I1 ≤ 0.80 mm (SOURCE YAGEO RC_L V.11), otherwise re-run check_gap (d); clean flux from around R1–R12; (2) ESD gun, ±4 kV contact on each pad E0–E11 of J2 with the device enumerated and playing; after each strike record whether the arc goes to the GND edge track or across a resistor, any I²C error, sensor-lost blink (REQ-009), USB disconnect or reset; (2b) strike the RV1 knob and, with the knob removed, the shaft tip, ±4 kV contact (R-011), recording the same effects plus the pot reading before and after; if the fitted shaft or knob is not the specified insulating type, record it and treat the result as not representative; record the wire length to RV1 and any metal enclosure; (3) after the series, measure every R1–R12 again; pass = every pad still detects touch and sends MIDI, RV1 still sweeps the full CC range, and every R1–R12 stays within 3234–3366 Ω (±2 %, ASSUMPTION from the 0.901 sensitivity at 3366 Ω, SIMULATION T-094); temporary upsets that recover without a power cycle are recorded, not a fail. A failure of (3), or an arc across a resistor in (2), is the plan-B trigger (R-018, ADR-027 D-2).

title: I2C hand-wire fault current
statement: A misplaced SDA or SCL hand wire (including one on a supply pad S1/S2/S6/S7) shall not drive an RP2040 pad beyond its IO current limits.
evidence: I: 220 Ω series resistors are present between the Pico pads and the bus: pad 31 SDA_PICO → R16 → SDA, pad 32 SCL_PICO → R15 → SCL (interface_check `fw.pcb.PIN_SDA/SCL_vs_pcb`). A: fault current 15.5 mA per line at 3.4 V, 30.9 mA for both lines, ≤ IIOVDD_MAX 50 mA (SOURCE S-17 Table 625). Low-level margins: Pico→MPR121 0.138 V, MPR121→Pico 0.235 V (budgets B5/B6, CALCULATION). Statement reworded after ADR-009 D-9: a wire on a supply pad is still physically possible, but it is now current-limited.

title: Both module revisions
statement: One PCB shall accept both Adafruit 1982 revisions. JP1, a 3-pad surface solder bridge, connects ORIG (+3V3 → S1 = VIN) or QT (+3V3 → S7 = VCC). The SDA/SCL wires from the J1 surface pads go to S5/S6 (original) or S3/S4 (STEMMA QT).
evidence: I: PASS on the design file (T-093). interface_check `pcb.JP1_selector`, `pcb.JP1_smd_bridge`, `pcb.J1_J3_smd` (SMD pads, no holes), `pcb.J1` (J1 1 = SCL, 2 = SDA). hardware/README.md section 5 table (JP1, SDA, SCL) = ORIG/S5/S6 and QT/S3/S4, which matches the Eagle-derived S-row (`doc.hw_readme.jp1_and_wires.*`). pcb_rules_check: JP1 pad gap 1.87 mm against the 1.8 mm rule, mutation-tested. Change from V1.2: the board has no silkscreen (ADR-023), so ORIG and QT are etched in copper and the longer legend 'ORIG = no white connectors', 'QT = 2 white connectors' exists only on the assembly map (`pcb.JP1_legend`, F.Fab); see REQ-040 and risk R-007. T-103: A2 lands now 1.8 × 4.2 mm (electrode row) and 1.8 × 5.515 mm (S row, joined to its J3 pad), 1.73–1.775 mm beyond the module outline, so the 20 butted joints are soldered and inspected from outside (F3-001; pcb_rules_check land table PASS). The ORIG label is etched left of JP1 beside the pad 2–1 gap; the hardware README describes that position (ADR-028 D-2), the manual still says 'below' (REQ-036). Module height and pin assumptions: first-build list in REQ-029. T: NOT RUN.

title: I2C rise time (PCB)
statement: The PCB-build I2C bus shall meet the rise time for its clock: ≤ 300 ns at 400 kHz (≤ 1000 ns at 100 kHz), with the module at 0x5A.
evidence: A: PASS. R13/R14 4.7 kΩ: t_r 156 ns at 60 pF, C_b limit 115.2 pF (systems, with RPU 80 kΩ from S-17); electronics gives 103 ns at 38 pF. The 220 Ω series resistors add 2.2 ns (ASSUMPTION of 10 pF pad capacitance). IO levels with 220 Ω: B5–B8 PASS, minimum margin 0.138 V (S-17 Table 625, S-04 Table 5). T: NOT RUN (plan item P-4).

title: Single-layer SMD PCB
statement: The PCB shall have copper on one layer only, F.Cu (the component side), and carry surface-mount parts only. The only holes shall be the 4 M3 mounting holes. There shall be no vias and no copper pour. The only wire links shall be the 2 I2C configuration links (J1 SCL/SDA to the S-row pads of J3); JP1 is a solder bridge on etched pads.
evidence: I: PASS on the design file (T-104, T-103 board on fd7140b). pcb_rules_check `SUMMARY: 26 checks, 26 PASS, 0 FAIL`: 0 B.Cu objects, 0 vias, 0 copper zones (3 keep-out rule areas, the third for the Pico 2 TP7), 127 SMD pads on F.Cu with no drill, 121 F.Cu segments, 4 M3 NPTH holes on H1..H4 matching the 4 hits of the drill file, every multi-pad net one F.Cu island (SW1 pads joined inside the switch only), J1 only SCL/SDA. Every check was mutation-tested on a scratch copy (management/handoffs/systems-engineer/T-104/mutation_results.txt, `MUTATION SUMMARY: 85 proved, 0 not proved`). A design-file check: no board has been etched or drilled.

title: Board outline
statement: The board outline shall be 100 × 70 mm.
evidence: Outline 100.000 × 70.000 mm (sim/systems/pcb_rules_check.out, T-093: `PASS  REQ-028 board outline 100 x 70 mm`). Board label 'FrutaMIDI v1.3' etched on F.Cu (ADR-023): interface_check `PASS  pcb.label_v1.3`. The label is not part of this requirement's statement.

title: Home-etch and SMD land rules
statement: Home-etch rules: signal tracks ≥ 1.0 mm (≥ 0.8 mm for short stubs up to 6 mm), power tracks ≥ 1.2 mm, clearance between nets ≥ 0.6 mm (DRC hard minimum 0.5 mm), copper ≥ 0.5 mm from the board edge. SMD lands shall be ≥ 1.0 mm in both directions and match the v1.3 land table after T-103 (A1 1.6 × 4.2 mm, A2 1.8 × 4.2 mm electrode row and 1.8 × 5.515 mm S row, J2 3.0 × 4.5 mm, JP1 1.94 × 2.4 mm at pitch 3.81 mm, gap ≥ 1.8 mm, R1–R12 1.9 × 3.35 mm, R13–R16 1.775 × 1.8 mm, C1 1.875 × 1.8 mm, SW1 1.55 × 1.3 mm, RV1 3.0 mm, J1 2.2 mm, J3 1.8 mm), with no bare copper in the 3 Pico keep-out areas. The Pico end shall be inside the board edge and the USB receptacle face ≥ 1.0 mm beyond it (ADR-028 D-1). The remaining holes shall be drilled ≥ 0.8 mm with copper ≥ 0.5 mm from the hole edge. The annular-ring rule no longer applies because no plated hole remains.
evidence: I + A PASS on the design file (T-104, T-103 board on fd7140b). pcb_rules_check `SUMMARY: 26 checks, 26 PASS, 0 FAIL`: track widths 0.8/1.0/1.2 mm, 0.8 mm only on 5 stubs (longest 5.08 mm), power ≥ 1.2 mm; minimum copper clearance between nets 0.680 mm (C1.2 to the SCL_PICO track, MEASUREMENT, pads and tracks; etched text left to DRC); nearest copper 0.680 mm from the board edge at A1 pin 1 (rule 0.5 mm); land table after T-103 and ≥ 1.0 mm rule PASS (smallest 1.30 mm); 0 copper items in the 3 keep-out areas; Pico end 0.11 mm inside the edge and USB face 1.19 mm beyond it (`ADR-028 D-1`, limit 1.0 mm ASSUMPTION; accepted 0.11 mm short of flush, ADR-028 D-1); JP1 gap 1.87 mm; J2 pads 3.0 × 4.5 mm; hole clearance; spark gap (ADR-020) 1.400 mm on E0–E11. Electronics check_smd (T-103) adds: every hand-soldered land ≥ 1.0 mm of copper outside the body or strip (A1 1.79, A2 1.73, SW1 1.65, R1 1.17, R13 1.05, C1 1.05 mm) and copper ≥ 0.6 mm from all 11 Pico 2 underside features (worst 2.14 mm) (MEASUREMENT on the design file, reports/electronics/evidence/T-103/). Every systems check was mutation-tested (management/handoffs/systems-engineer/T-104/mutation_results.txt). The rules do not prove that the lands can be etched or hand-soldered (R-003, R-013, R-014): user trial etch and solder are NOT RUN. First-build measurement list (T-103 build ASSUMPTIONS, each to be measured on the first build, [PHYSICAL], NOT RUN): (1) height of the supplied header strip, assumed 2.5 mm; (2) exposed pin length after cutting, set to 3.0 mm, all 20 equal; (3) Adafruit module board thickness, assumed 1.6 mm, giving the module underside about 5.5 mm and its top about 7.1 mm above the copper; (4) C1 body, assumed up to 3.4 × 1.8 mm (Samsung datasheet not opened), and the 1.0 mm copper beyond it; (5) B3S body 6.0 + 0.1 mm; (6) cut and transfer tolerance, assumed 1.0 mm (0.5 transfer + 0.5 trim): measure the USB receptacle face beyond the trimmed edge (design 1.19 mm, limit 1.0 mm) and that the Pico end is inside the edge (design 0.11 mm, ADR-028 D-1); (7) one RC2512 body L and termination I1 (REQ-023 step 1). If a value falls outside its assumption, re-run check_smd and pcb_rules_check with the measured value.

title: Electrode wire pads
statement: The PCB shall provide 14 solder-wire pads at 5.08 mm pitch: GND, E0..E11, GND. Pad k (k = 2..13) shall reach MPR121 electrode k − 2 through its series resistor.
evidence: interface_check `pcb.J2.T1..T14`, `pcb.A2.pin2..13`, `pcb.J2_solder_pads`, and pcb_rules_check `ADR-023 J2 is 14 SMD solder-wire pads` PASS (T-093). The project definition was amended for CR-003 (management/PROJECT_DEFINITION.md amendment of 2026-11-09, commit 410933d); its older screw-terminal line is superseded by that amendment. Strength of the wire joints and hot-melt relief is NOT RUN (R-013).

title: Pin map consistency
statement: The firmware PCB pin map (I2C1 SDA GP26 / SCL GP27, button GP22, pot GP28/ADC2) shall match the PCB nets. The breadboard map (I2C0 GP4/GP5, button GP15, pot GP26) shall match README.md.
evidence: interface_check: 0 pin mismatches.

title: Core BOM cost
statement: The core BOM (assembled board, excluding tools, consumables and USB cable) shall cost ≤ 30 EUR.
evidence: A: PASS on the basis ruled by ADR-027 D-1 (core BOM excluding shipping, consumables and tools, as in every earlier revision). Core 14.84–16.84 EUR ex VAT (CALCULATION, sim/systems/budgets.out revision 9, `PASS  C1 core BOM upper bound <= 30 EUR (ex VAT, ex shipping) :: core 14.84 .. 16.84 EUR`), margin 13.16 EUR at the upper bound. title: JP1 wrong-position tolerance
statement: A wrong JP1 position (ORIG on a STEMMA QT module, or QT on an original module), or both sides bridged, shall not apply a voltage outside the MPR121 absolute maximum ratings (inputs ≤ VDD + 0.3 V, S-04 Table 3), and shall not short +3V3 through a module output.
